sources.entry: How To Invest In Startups - Sam Altman

summary.title: How To Invest In Startups
summary.one_liner: Sam Altman's framework for startup investing: get access to deals by working hard, pick great founders and markets, and win allocations by being decisive and founder-friendly.
takeaways: Successful investing needs three things: access to good deals, good decisions about what to invest in, and getting companies to choose you as an investor.
Look for founders who are scrappy and formidable, fast-moving, extremely smart, and able to improve quickly; the rate of improvement matters more than current ability.
Focus on markets with fast growth and eventual size rather than current size, and aim for opportunities that could be $10 billion companies.
Win deals by being decisive, treating founders as peers, and building a founder-friendly reputation; help founders mainly by raising their ambition and giving tactical advice.
summary.summary: This essay by Sam Altman gives his personal advice on early-stage startup investing, organized around three areas: access, decisions, and close rate. It also covers how to help founders after investing. The piece is opinion-based and draws on his own experience rather than data or a formal method. It is short and conversational, with lists of traits and examples such as the iPhone to illustrate points.
